question: Bank A pays 4.00% once a year. Bank B pays 3.95% a year, credited monthly. Which earns more over a year?
answer: Bank B, just. Monthly credits earn interest on interest: (1 + 0.0395 ÷ 12)¹² ≈ 1.0402, an annual equivalent rate of 4.02%. That is what the AER quoted on UK savings accounts does: it folds the compounding into one number you can compare.
move: Compare savings by the yearly equivalent rate, not the headline rate.
ask: Which two rates have I compared that were compounded on different schedules?
trap: Bank A, because 4.00 is bigger than 3.95.
source: Financial Conduct Authority, Handbook glossary, annual equivalent rate
reference: Financial Conduct Authority, FCA Handbook glossary: annual equivalent rate (AER), 2024
